full_judgment: 11. Mr. Murad Reza, learned Additional Attorney General appearing for the respondent-Government, at the outset, has referred to several decisions of the apex courts of our sub-continent, namely the decisions reported in 41 DLR (AD)-30, 27 DLR(AD)-60, PLD 1958 (Peshawar)-73 and 50 DLR (AD)-27. Mr. Reza submits that there is always a strong presumption in favour of any action of the statutory bodies as regards the constitutionality or legality of the same and it is the burden of the persons who allege illegality to substantiate such illegality. According to him, since the petitioners have so far failed to show any such illegality or unconstitutionality to rebut such strong presumption, the Rules should be discharged. Mr. Reza further argues that when in a particular statutory provision words are unambiguous and clear, nothing is left for the Court to give interpretation of the same relying on any extraneous matters, and the court should stick to the intention of the legislature as expressed by the said unambiguous words of that provision. He then argues that since the words under section 2CC are very much clear and unambiguous, and the impugned notifications issued under section 2CC being also not ambiguous, the petitioners do not have any case to argue before this court. As regards the argument of inconsistency of the impugned notification with section 27 Ka of the Companies Act 1991 Mr. Reza submits that it is the established rule of interpretation that when there is any conflict between two provisions of two statutes, the court should endeavour to give harmonious interpretation and try to save both the provisions.
